title: Part Squares
description: Number the whole squares inside a traced shape, mark each part square by its kind, pair the half squares, and give the area as an estimate with about.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

writeup.why: Estimate the area of a curved or irregular shape on squared paper: number the whole squares, count a square more than half covered as one and leave out one less than half covered, pair the half squares, and give the total with about.
writeup.look: A traced outline on squared paper with every square it touches waiting to be marked, and a tally card at the right that ends on about.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Part Squares' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of squares marked. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The squared paper fills a box 640 by 440 at x 120, y 230, each cell 40 across, with the traced outline in near-black ink. A whole square takes its number in violet, labelled Unit square. A square more than half inside turns rose with the words More than half written in it; a square cut in half turns a paler rose with the word Half; a square less than half inside stays warm white with the words Less than half in small ink. No square is ever marked with a cross. The Pair button stands at x 820, y 250, and a pair is drawn as a thin ink bracket joining two Half squares. The tally card stands at x 820, y 330, 280 by 300, with the lines Whole, More than half, Half pairs and Left out, and a total line that begins with the word about. The estimate reached is green. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with an sq. cm key. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the ten tools of this chapter share them. The lengths the question gives, as a side, a length, a breadth, a height, an edge or a base area, are deep blue, labelled Given or by their own name. The perimeter, area, volume or missing side the working reaches is green, labelled Answer. The boundary that a perimeter walks round is vermilion, labelled Boundary. The unit being counted, one unit square, one unit cube, one row or one layer, is violet, labelled Unit square, Unit cube, Row or Layer. The part squares of an estimate and the space left over where no whole cube fits are rose, labelled More than half, Half or Left over. The side, square, cube, layer or step being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open, and nothing on this stage is ever grey. A square or cube that is not being counted stays warm white inside its near-black outline, grid lines, unit words and signs are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of them, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The last outline stays with every square marked by its kind, and the tally card beside it ends on about and the area in green.

phases.win: the last whole square reads 18, and the tally's Whole line reads 18
phases.does: taps each whole square in turn, row by row, and types the last number written
phases.goal: count the whole squares inside an outline first, numbering each one so none is counted twice

writeup.delight: On the fourth phase, when the total lands, the word about gives a small bow before it, and the traced hand gives a little wave.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet marked. On the first phase a traced leaf lies on squared paper with its whole squares blank. On the second the same leaf's edge squares wait unmarked. On the third a shape lies whose outline cuts squares in half, with the Pair button beside it. On the fourth a traced hand lies with its squares already marked and the tally card waiting. One thing moves, once: the first square to be tapped, or the tally card on the fourth phase, gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any traced outline, or a figure along the grid lines, marked square by square and tallied. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on whole squares, the rules for part squares, pairing halves and estimates.

Tap each whole square once. Give it a number as you go.
Is more than half of this square inside the line?

Add them by the rules. Then say about.

Free play. Trace any shape and sort its squares.
Look at that square again. How much of it is inside the line?
You estimated an area, and said about.

voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

items.planQuestion: A traced leaf has rows of 2, 7, 5 and 4 whole squares. How many whole squares does it hold?

question.en: How many whole squares does this leaf hold, if you number each as you tap it?

items.planQuestion: A traced shape has rows of 3, 6 and 5 whole squares. How many whole squares is that?

question.en: How many whole squares does this second leaf hold?
How many whole squares are inside this small leaf?

items.planQuestion: Round a traced shape, 7 squares are more than half covered and 3 are less than half covered. How many whole squares do they add?

question.en: How many whole squares do the M squares add, once each edge is marked?

items.planQuestion: A square on the outline is more than half covered. How is it counted?

question.en: How many whole squares is the ringed square counted as?

items.planQuestion: Round a traced cup, 9 squares are more than half covered and 5 are less than half covered. How many whole squares do they add?

question.en: How many whole squares do the edge squares round this traced cup count for?

items.planAnswer: 9. The 9 count as 9, and the 5 less-than-half squares are left out

items.planQuestion: An outline cuts 10 squares exactly in half. How many whole squares do they make?

question.en: How many whole squares do the half squares of this shape make?

items.planQuestion: How many whole squares do 14 half squares make?

question.en: This outline cuts 14 squares in half, so how many whole squares is that?

items.planAnswer: 7, because two half squares make 1 whole square

items.planQuestion: A square is cut from corner to corner by the outline. How is it counted?

question.en: How many whole squares do these 6 corner to corner halves come to?

items.planAnswer: As a half square, because a cut from corner to corner splits it exactly in half

items.planQuestion: A traced hand has 21 whole squares, 9 more-than-half squares and 6 half squares. What is its area?

question.en: After pairing the halves, what is the area of this traced hand in squares?

items.planQuestion: A traced leaf has 13 whole squares, 5 more-than-half squares and 4 half squares. What is its area?

question.en: Once its halves are paired, roughly what area does this leaf cover?

items.planAnswer: The 4 half squares make 2. 13 + 5 + 2 = 20, so the leaf is about 20 sq. cm

items.planQuestion: A traced stone has 16 whole squares, 7 more-than-half squares, 6 half squares and 4 less-than-half squares. What is its area?

question.en: About how many squares does this traced stone cover?

items.planAnswer: The 6 half squares make 3, and the 4 less-than-half squares are left out. 16 + 7 + 3 = 26, so the stone is about 26 sq. cm

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.
